headline: Nifty Crosses 23,200 While Sensex Ends Lower Amid Saudi Supply Concerns
why: Saudi Aramco halted crude supplies following a major pipeline attack
IT sector weakness dragged indices despite gains in other sectors
Indian bonds suffered a fifth weekly loss due to RBI moves
Strong direct tax collection data provided a fiscal cushion for markets
whatHappening: Nifty 50 closed above 23,200 while Sensex ended 22 points lower
Net direct tax collections reached ₹12.12 lakh crore by mid-September
Rupee remained stable at 95.89 against the US dollar today
India announced the 2027 launch of the Qdenga dengue vaccine

stocksInNews.sources: Saudi Aramco halts crude supplies to Indian refiners
IT sector drags market performance ahead of Fed call
India bonds face fifth weekly loss on RBI moves
IT stocks under pressure despite broader market gains
Sensex recovers 333 points in late trade session
Net direct tax collection rises 13 percent to 12.12 lakh crore
Nifty gains 53 points to close above 23,200 level
FMCG sector shines as market snaps two-day losing streak
Bhumika Realty retail lease signals strong commercial demand
Crude supply disruption from Saudi Aramco impacts auto sentiment

summary: The Indian stock market ended mixed as Nifty surpassed the 23,200 mark despite Sensex volatility. Concerns over Saudi crude supply disruptions were partially offset by strong domestic direct tax collection data. Metals and FMCG sectors led the gains while IT stocks faced significant selling pressure.
